newsitem.title: USA: U.S. considers punitive action against Iran -report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. considers punitive action against Iran -report.

text.p: The United States is planning possible punitive action against Iran if it is proven to be behind a bomb attack that killed 19 U.S. airmen in Saudi Arabia, the Los Angeles Times reported on Thursday.
The newspaper said U.S. law enforcement and Pentagon officials have tentatively concluded that Saudi Shiites were responsible for the June 20 attack on a military housing complex in Dhahran.
But the Los Angeles Times said that the U.S. government lacked sufficient proof to support Saudi Arabia's contention that Shiites trained and armed by Iran carried out the truck bombing.
"A lot of people would like to bash Iran and the Saudi case fuels their desire to do it," a senior U.S. law enforcement official told the paper.
"But any conclusion, not to mention any action, is very premature," he added.

The Times said the officials cautioned that Iran and Syria were tentatively thought responsible for the 1988 bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland -- a belief later found to be wrong. Two Libyans have been named as suspects in that attack.
The newspaper said the possible punitive actions planned included retaliatory strikes on Iranian military targets.
A Pentagon spokesman had no immediate comment on the report.

The Washington Post reported on Wednesday that Saudi Arabia had given the United States detailed data to support the Saudis' belief that the bombing was carried out by Shiite extremists trained in Lebanon and backed by Iran.
The data included confessions extracted from some of 40 Saudi Shiites detained and accused of involvement in the June bombing, the Post said.

Iran's U.N. mission on Wednesday denied the reports implying Iranian involvement in the bombing. It said the press reports were "invariably based on conjectures and cynical speculations" and were devoid of any specific attribution or evidence.
